children: Tropical Storm Edouard is nearing the U.S. Gulf Coast Tuesday afternoon, according to the latest update from the National Hurricane Center released around 2 p.m. ET.

The storm continued to sustain windspeeds of about 50 mph, short of the 74 mph minimum speed for a Category 1 hurricane. Tropical storm warnings continue from Port Bolivar, Texas, to the Vermilion/Iberia Parish line in Louisiana.
With the storm nearing landfall beneath hurricane-force winds, the hurricane watch has been discontinued. Additionally, the storm surge warnings have also been discontinued.

As of 2 p.m. ET, the storm was still moving northwest at 8 mph and expected to continue at the speed through Wednesday morning. The storm is expected to reach the coast later Tuesday and move inland over southeast Texas later Tuesday night. Rapid weakening of the storm is expected as the center moves onto land.
Tropical storm-force winds are expected to still extend 25 miles from the center, according to the NHC.

According to the latest update, tropical storm-force winds are already beginning to spread into the region. A National Ocean Service station at Calcasieu Pass, La., recorded sustained winds of 44 mph and a gust of 52 mph.

The storm is expected to produce 3-6 inches of rain with a maximum total of 9 inches for parts of the upper Texas coast inland through east-central Texas. In southwest Louisiana, rain totals are expected to be 2-4 inches.
So far, there have been no reports of any impact on refineries or facilities in the area and little reaction in Gulf Coast spot market trading.
NHC will issue another update at 5 p.m. ET.
